issues.description: delimiter argument conflates literal characters and OpenAPI style names in one namespace.
issues.detail: The delimiter parameter accepts both raw characters (',', '|', ' ') and symbolic style names ('pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited') through one keyword. These are two disjoint concepts sharing one key space, making the precondition awkward to state and giving callers two ways to express the same intent. Separate the vocabularies or pick one.

issues.description: ValueError for unsupported delimiter conflicts with the HTTPBadRequest convention.
issues.detail: get_param_as_list converts ValueError from transforms into HTTPBadRequest for client input errors. Raising plain ValueError for a developer-supplied bad delimiter risks being reported to the client as 400, mixing programmer error with malformed client input on the same channel. Use TypeError or a precondition assertion to separate the failure modes.

issues.description: Delimiter validation is lazy rather than checked once at entry.
issues.detail: An invalid delimiter only raises when the param happens to be present; a missing param with a typo'd delimiter silently returns default. The set of legal delimiters is known at definition time and should be validated at the boundary, not intertwined with request handling. Move the membership check above the `if name in params` block.

issues.description: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS conflates identity mappings with alias mappings.
issues.detail: Three of five entries map a character to itself; only two are genuine aliases. A cleaner decomposition is an allowlist set {',', '|', ' '} plus an alias dict {'pipeDelimited': '|', 'spaceDelimited': ' '}. This makes the precondition expressible in one line and the table self-explanatory.

issues.description: Silent no-op when items is already a list erodes the delimiter contract.
issues.detail: When the same parameter appears multiple times, items is already a list and delimiter is silently discarded. A caller requesting `delimiter='|'` on `?x=a|b&x=c|d` gets `['a|b','c|d']` unsplit. The postcondition (split iff scalar, else as-is) should be either honored uniformly or stated as a contract, not left as a Note.

issues.description: Tests demonstrate happy paths but miss boundary cases and the default+delimiter interaction.
issues.detail: Tests cover the four documented examples and one rejection, but omit empty values, trailing delimiters, keep_blank_qs_values interaction, single token with no delimiter, and crucially get_param_as_list('missing', delimiter='pipeDelimited', default=[...]). The last would pin the lazy-validation contract. Spec remains demonstrated rather than proved.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature is small, localized, and correct on its happy paths, but under-specified at its edges. The core complaint across all three reviewers is that the `delimiter` parameter mixes two vocabularies — literal characters and OpenAPI style names — in one keyword and one lookup table whose entries are half identity, half alias. Two reviewers also flag that raising plain `ValueError` for a programmer-supplied bad delimiter conflates developer error with malformed client input given the HTTPBadRequest convention. Validation is lazy rather than checked at the boundary, and the test suite demonstrates examples rather than establishing the invariant. Land-able with the noted cleanups.
